title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
authors: Shannon CE
summary: Founded information theory and introduced n-gram (Markov) approximations of English text, the conceptual ancestor of statistical language modeling.

title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
authors: Turing AM
summary: Proposed the imitation game (Turing test), framing machine intelligence in terms of natural-language conversation.

title: Distributional Structure
authors: Harris ZS
summary: Articulated the distributional hypothesis that words occurring in similar contexts have similar meanings, the basis of later vector semantics.

title: Syntactic Structures
authors: Chomsky N
summary: Introduced transformational generative grammar and formal language hierarchies, reshaping linguistics and early symbolic NLP.

title: ELIZA—A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language Communication between Man and Machine
authors: Weizenbaum J
summary: Pattern-matching chatbot that simulated a Rogerian therapist, the first widely known conversational program and an early lesson in anthropomorphism.

title: Understanding Natural Language
authors: Winograd T
summary: Described SHRDLU, a system that understood and executed English commands in a blocks world by integrating syntax, semantics and reasoning.

title: A Stochastic Parts Program and Noun Phrase Parser for Unrestricted Text
authors: Church KW
venue: Proc. 2nd Conference on Applied Natural Language Processing (ANLP 1988)
summary: Showed that a simple HMM-style statistical tagger trained on corpora achieves high part-of-speech accuracy, helping launch the empirical turn in NLP.

title: A Tutorial on Hidden Markov Models and Selected Applications in Speech Recognition
authors: Rabiner LR
summary: Canonical exposition of HMM inference and training (forward-backward, Viterbi, Baum-Welch), the workhorse of speech and tagging for decades.

title: Indexing by Latent Semantic Analysis
authors: Deerwester S, Dumais ST, Furnas GW, Landauer TK, Harshman R
venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science 41(6):391-407
summary: Used truncated SVD of term-document matrices to obtain latent semantic vectors, an early dense distributional representation for retrieval.

title: The Mathematics of Statistical Machine Translation: Parameter Estimation
authors: Brown PF, Della Pietra SA, Della Pietra VJ, Mercer RL
summary: Defined IBM Models 1-5 for word alignment and translation trained with EM, the foundation of SMT for two decades.

title: Building a Large Annotated Corpus of English: The Penn Treebank
authors: Marcus MP, Santorini B, Marcinkiewicz MA
summary: Released a large POS-tagged and syntactically bracketed corpus that became the standard training and benchmark resource for tagging and parsing.

title: Improved Backing-off for M-gram Language Modeling
authors: Kneser R, Ney H
summary: Introduced Kneser-Ney smoothing, which uses continuation counts for lower-order distributions and became the best-performing n-gram smoothing method.

title: Conditional Random Fields: Probabilistic Models for Segmenting and Labeling Sequence Data
authors: Lafferty J, McCallum A, Pereira F
summary: Introduced CRFs, globally normalized discriminative sequence models that avoid label bias and dominated tagging and NER before neural methods.

title: BLEU: a Method for Automatic Evaluation of Machine Translation
authors: Papineni K, Roukos S, Ward T, Zhu WJ
summary: Proposed BLEU, an n-gram precision metric with a brevity penalty that became the standard automatic MT evaluation measure.

title: Statistical Phrase-Based Translation
authors: Koehn P, Och FJ, Marcu D
summary: Phrase-based SMT translating multi-word segments, which became the dominant MT paradigm until neural MT.

title: Latent Dirichlet Allocation
authors: Blei DM, Ng AY, Jordan MI
summary: Bayesian generative topic model representing documents as mixtures of topics, the standard tool for unsupervised text exploration.

title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model
authors: Bengio Y, Ducharme R, Vincent P, Jauvin C
summary: Jointly learned distributed word embeddings and a neural network n-gram language model, beating smoothed n-grams and founding neural language modeling.

title: Recurrent Neural Network Based Language Model
authors: Mikolov T, Karafiát M, Burget L, Černocký J, Khudanpur S
summary: Showed recurrent neural language models substantially reduce perplexity and speech recognition error versus n-gram models.

title: Natural Language Processing (Almost) from Scratch
authors: Collobert R, Weston J, Bottou L, Karlen M, Kavukcuoglu K, Kuksa P
summary: A unified neural architecture with pretrained word embeddings learned from unlabeled text that matched feature-engineered systems on tagging, chunking, NER and SRL.

title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
authors: Mikolov T, Chen K, Corrado G, Dean J
summary: Introduced word2vec (CBOW and skip-gram), cheap log-linear models whose embeddings capture semantic and syntactic analogies at scale.

title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
authors: Mikolov T, Sutskever I, Chen K, Corrado G, Dean J
summary: Added negative sampling, frequent-word subsampling and phrase vectors to skip-gram, making word2vec the standard embedding method.

title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
authors: Pennington J, Socher R, Manning CD
summary: Learned word vectors by weighted least-squares factorization of global co-occurrence counts, unifying count-based and predictive embeddings.

title: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
authors: Bojanowski P, Grave E, Joulin A, Mikolov T
summary: fastText: represented words as bags of character n-grams, giving embeddings for rare and unseen words and morphologically rich languages.

title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
authors: Howard J, Ruder S
summary: ULMFiT showed that pretraining an LSTM language model and fine-tuning it with careful schedules transfers strongly to text classification.

title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
authors: Peters ME, Neumann M, Iyyer M, Gardner M, Clark C, Lee K, Zettlemoyer L
summary: ELMo: contextual word representations from a deep bidirectional LSTM language model, delivering large gains across NLP tasks and heralding pretraining.

title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
authors: Cho K, van Merriënboer B, Gulcehre C, Bahdanau D, Bougares F, Schwenk H, Bengio Y
summary: Introduced the RNN encoder-decoder and the gated recurrent unit (GRU) for scoring phrase translations.

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
authors: Sutskever I, Vinyals O, Le QV
summary: Showed deep LSTM encoder-decoders map input to output sequences end to end, achieving competitive MT and establishing the seq2seq paradigm.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
authors: Bahdanau D, Cho K, Bengio Y
summary: Introduced soft attention letting the decoder align to encoder states, removing the fixed-vector bottleneck; the origin of attention in NLP.

title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation
authors: Luong MT, Pham H, Manning CD
summary: Systematized global and local attention with multiplicative scoring, simplifying and improving attentional NMT.

title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
authors: Sennrich R, Haddow B, Birch A
summary: Adapted byte-pair encoding for open-vocabulary subword tokenization, now the basis of tokenizers in nearly all LLMs.

title: Google's Neural Machine Translation System: Bridging the Gap between Human and Machine Translation
authors: Wu Y, Schuster M, Chen Z, Le QV, Norouzi M, Macherey W, et al.
summary: GNMT: deep LSTM attention model with wordpieces deployed in Google Translate, marking neural MT's production takeover from phrase-based SMT.

title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Vaswani A, Shazeer N, Parmar N, Uszkoreit J, Jones L, Gomez AN, et al.
summary: Introduced the Transformer, relying solely on multi-head self-attention, enabling parallel training and becoming the architecture of essentially all modern language models.

title: A Large Annotated Corpus for Learning Natural Language Inference
authors: Bowman SR, Angeli G, Potts C, Manning CD
summary: SNLI: 570k human-written premise-hypothesis pairs that made natural language inference a central neural benchmark.

title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
authors: Rajpurkar P, Zhang J, Lopyrev K, Liang P
summary: Large extractive reading-comprehension dataset over Wikipedia that drove rapid progress in neural QA and pretrained models.

title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
authors: Radford A, Narasimhan K, Salimans T, Sutskever I
summary: GPT-1: generative pretraining of a Transformer decoder followed by discriminative fine-tuning, establishing the pretrain-then-fine-tune Transformer recipe.

title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding
authors: Wang A, Singh A, Michael J, Hill F, Levy O, Bowman SR
summary: Nine-task NLU benchmark with a single leaderboard that became the yardstick for pretrained encoders such as BERT.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
authors: Devlin J, Chang MW, Lee K, Toutanova K
summary: Pretrained a bidirectional Transformer encoder with masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction, setting new records on GLUE and SQuAD and defining the pretrained-encoder era.

title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
authors: Radford A, Wu J, Child R, Luan D, Amodei D, Sutskever I
summary: GPT-2: a 1.5B-parameter decoder trained on WebText that performed many tasks zero-shot, showing scale alone yields broad capabilities.

title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems
authors: Wang A, Pruksachatkun Y, Nangia N, Singh A, Michael J, Hill F, et al.
summary: Harder successor to GLUE created after pretrained models surpassed human baselines on the original benchmark.

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
authors: Liu Y, Ott M, Goyal N, Du J, Joshi M, Chen D, et al.
summary: Showed BERT was undertrained; more data, longer training, dynamic masking and dropping NSP gave large gains.

title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding
authors: Yang Z, Dai Z, Yang Y, Carbonell J, Salakhutdinov R, Le QV
summary: Permutation language modeling combining autoregressive training with bidirectional context, outperforming BERT on many benchmarks.

title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
authors: Lewis M, Liu Y, Goyal N, Ghazvininejad M, Mohamed A, Levy O, et al.
summary: Denoising autoencoder pretraining for an encoder-decoder Transformer, strong for summarization and generation.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
authors: Raffel C, Shazeer N, Roberts A, Lee K, Narang S, Matena M, et al.
summary: T5: cast every NLP task as text-to-text, released the C4 corpus and systematically studied pretraining objectives and scale.

title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators
authors: Clark K, Luong MT, Le QV, Manning CD
summary: Replaced-token detection pretraining that is far more compute-efficient than masked language modeling.

title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
authors: Shoeybi M, Patwary M, Puri R, LeGresley P, Casper J, Catanzaro B
summary: Intra-layer tensor model parallelism for Transformers that enabled efficient training of multi-billion-parameter language models.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
authors: Brown TB, Mann B, Ryder N, Subbiah M, Kaplan J, Dhariwal P, et al.
summary: GPT-3: a 175B-parameter language model demonstrating in-context few-shot learning from prompts alone, launching the large language model era.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
authors: Chen M, Tworek J, Jun H, Yuan Q, Pinto HPdO, Kaplan J, et al.
summary: Introduced Codex and the HumanEval benchmark, showing code-trained LLMs can synthesize functional programs from docstrings.

title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
authors: Fedus W, Zoph B, Shazeer N
summary: Simplified mixture-of-experts routing to top-1 experts, training trillion-parameter sparse language models efficiently.

title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
authors: Chowdhery A, Narang S, Devlin J, Bosma M, Mishra G, Roberts A, et al.
summary: A 540B dense Transformer trained on Pathways showing breakthrough few-shot and chain-of-thought reasoning performance.

title: Introducing ChatGPT
authors: OpenAI
summary: Public release of an RLHF-tuned conversational GPT-3.5 model whose rapid adoption brought LLMs into mainstream use.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
authors: Touvron H, Lavril T, Izacard G, Martinet X, Lachaux MA, Lacroix T, et al.
summary: Openly released 7B-65B models trained compute-optimally on public data, matching much larger models and catalyzing the open-weight LLM ecosystem.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
authors: OpenAI
summary: Large multimodal model reaching human-level performance on many professional and academic exams, with predictable scaling of training outcomes.

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
authors: Touvron H, Martin L, Stone K, Albert P, Almahairi A, Babaei Y, et al.
summary: Open-weight 7B-70B base and RLHF-tuned chat models with detailed safety and alignment methodology, licensed for commercial use.

title: Qwen Technical Report
authors: Bai J, Bai S, Chu Y, Cui Z, Dang K, Deng X, et al.
summary: Alibaba's first Qwen open LLM family, beginning a leading line of multilingual open-weight models.

title: Mistral 7B
authors: Jiang AQ, Sablayrolles A, Mensch A, Bamford C, Chaplot DS, de las Casas D, et al.
summary: Compact open model using grouped-query and sliding-window attention that outperformed larger Llama 2 models.

title: Mixtral of Experts
authors: Jiang AQ, Sablayrolles A, Roux A, Mensch A, Savary B, Bamford C, et al.
summary: Open sparse mixture-of-experts model (8 experts, 2 active) matching much larger dense models at lower inference cost.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
authors: Dubey A, Jauhri A, Pandey A, Kadian A, Al-Dahle A, Letman A, et al.
summary: Open dense models up to 405B parameters trained on ~15T tokens, approaching frontier closed-model quality.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
authors: DeepSeek-AI
summary: 671B-parameter MoE model trained with FP8 and multi-token prediction for a fraction of typical frontier cost, rivaling leading closed models.

title: Qwen3 Technical Report
authors: Yang A, Li A, Yang B, Zhang B, Hui B, Zheng B, et al.
summary: Open dense and MoE models unifying thinking and non-thinking modes with a controllable reasoning budget.

title: Introducing GPT-5
authors: OpenAI
summary: Unified system routing between fast and extended-reasoning models, with strong coding and agentic tool-use performance.

title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences
authors: Ziegler DM, Stiennon N, Wu J, Brown TB, Radford A, Amodei D, et al.
summary: First application of reward modeling from human comparisons plus PPO to fine-tune pretrained language models.

title: Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback
authors: Stiennon N, Ouyang L, Wu J, Ziegler DM, Lowe R, Voss C, et al.
summary: Showed RLHF summarization policies outperform supervised models and larger references, demonstrating the RLHF recipe at scale.

title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
authors: Wei J, Bosma M, Zhao VY, Guu K, Yu AW, Lester B, et al.
summary: FLAN: instruction tuning on many tasks phrased as natural-language instructions markedly improves zero-shot performance on unseen tasks.

title: Multitask Prompted Training Enables Zero-Shot Task Generalization
authors: Sanh V, Webson A, Raffel C, Bach SH, Sutawika L, Alyafeai Z, et al.
summary: T0: multitask fine-tuning of T5 on a large collection of prompted datasets yields strong zero-shot generalization.

title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
authors: Ouyang L, Wu J, Jiang X, Almeida D, Wainwright CL, Mishkin P, et al.
summary: InstructGPT: supervised instruction tuning plus RLHF made a 1.3B model preferred over 175B GPT-3, the recipe behind ChatGPT.

title: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
authors: Chung HW, Hou L, Longpre S, Zoph B, Tay Y, Fedus W, et al.
summary: Flan-T5/Flan-PaLM: scaled instruction tuning to 1,800+ tasks with chain-of-thought data, improving many model families.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
authors: Bai Y, Kadavath S, Kundu S, Askell A, Kernion J, Jones A, et al.
summary: Trained harmless assistants using a written constitution and AI-generated critiques and preferences (RLAIF) instead of human harm labels.

title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
authors: Wang Y, Kordi Y, Mishra S, Liu A, Smith NA, Khashabi D, Hajishirzi H
summary: Bootstrapped instruction-tuning data from a model's own generations, inspiring cheap open instruction-tuned models like Alpaca.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
authors: Rafailov R, Sharma A, Mitchell E, Ermon S, Manning CD, Finn C
summary: Derived a closed-form classification loss that optimizes the RLHF objective directly from preferences without a separate reward model or RL.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
authors: Zheng L, Chiang WL, Sheng Y, Zhuang S, Wu Z, Zhuang Y, et al.
summary: Validated strong LLMs as scalable judges of chat quality and introduced MT-Bench and crowdsourced Chatbot Arena evaluation.

title: The Claude 3 Model Family: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku
authors: Anthropic
summary: Frontier multimodal assistant family trained with Constitutional AI and RLHF, emphasizing helpfulness, honesty and harmlessness.

title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted Question-Answering with Human Feedback
authors: Nakano R, Hilton J, Balaji S, Wu J, Ouyang L, Kim C, et al.
summary: Fine-tuned GPT-3 to search and browse a text web environment and cite sources, an early tool-using LLM agent trained with human feedback.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Wei J, Wang X, Schuurmans D, Bosma M, Ichter B, Xia F, et al.
summary: Showed that prompting with step-by-step reasoning exemplars dramatically improves LLM arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
authors: Wang X, Wei J, Schuurmans D, Le Q, Chi E, Narang S, et al.
summary: Sampled diverse reasoning paths and took a majority vote over answers, a simple and powerful early form of test-time compute.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
authors: Yao S, Zhao J, Yu D, Du N, Shafran I, Narasimhan K, Cao Y
summary: Interleaved reasoning traces with actions such as search calls, the template for modern LLM agents.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
authors: Schick T, Dwivedi-Yu J, Dessì R, Raileanu R, Lomeli M, Zettlemoyer L, et al.
summary: Self-supervised method for a model to learn when and how to call APIs such as calculators, search and translation.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
authors: Yao S, Yu D, Zhao J, Shafran I, Griffiths TL, Cao Y, Narasimhan K
summary: Generalized chain-of-thought to tree search over intermediate thoughts with self-evaluation and backtracking.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
authors: Lightman H, Kosaraju V, Burda Y, Edwards H, Baker B, Lee T, et al.
summary: Showed process supervision of each reasoning step trains better reward models than outcome supervision, releasing the PRM800K dataset.

title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
authors: Shao Z, Wang P, Zhu Q, Xu R, Song J, Bi X, et al.
summary: Introduced Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), a critic-free RL method later central to open reasoning models.

title: Learning to Reason with LLMs
authors: OpenAI
summary: o1 models trained with large-scale RL to produce long hidden chains of thought, showing performance scales with test-time reasoning compute.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
authors: Snell C, Lee J, Xu K, Kumar A
summary: Analyzed compute-optimal allocation of inference-time search and revision, showing test-time compute can substitute for model scale.

title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
authors: Yang J, Jimenez CE, Wettig A, Lieret K, Yao S, Narasimhan K, Press O
summary: Showed purpose-built agent-computer interfaces let LLM agents navigate repositories and fix real GitHub issues.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
authors: Jimenez CE, Yang J, Wettig A, Yao S, Pei K, Press O, Narasimhan K
summary: Benchmark of real GitHub issues from Python repositories, verified by unit tests, that became the main yardstick for coding agents.

title: Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku
authors: Anthropic
summary: First frontier model offered with general computer use, operating desktop GUIs via screenshots, mouse and keyboard actions.

title: Model Context Protocol
authors: Anthropic
summary: Open protocol standardizing how LLM applications connect to tools and data sources, widely adopted across agent frameworks.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
authors: DeepSeek-AI
summary: Showed pure RL with verifiable rewards (GRPO) elicits long chain-of-thought reasoning; released open reasoning weights and distilled models rivaling o1.

title: Introducing Claude 4
authors: Anthropic
summary: Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 hybrid-reasoning models targeted at long-running agentic coding, leading SWE-bench at release.

title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
authors: Hendrycks D, Burns C, Basart S, Zou A, Mazeika M, Song D, Steinhardt J
summary: MMLU: 57-subject multiple-choice exam benchmark that became the headline measure of LLM knowledge.

title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
authors: Liang P, Bommasani R, Lee T, Tsipras D, Soylu D, Yasunaga M, et al.
summary: HELM: standardized multi-metric evaluation of many LLMs across scenarios, covering accuracy, calibration, robustness, bias and efficiency.

title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
authors: Robertson S, Zaragoza H
venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval 3(4):333-389
summary: Definitive account of the probabilistic relevance model and BM25, still the standard sparse retrieval baseline.

title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
authors: Hinton G, Vinyals O, Dean J
summary: Knowledge distillation: training a small student on a large teacher's softened outputs, widely used to compress language models.

title: DistilBERT, a Distilled Version of BERT: Smaller, Faster, Cheaper and Lighter
authors: Sanh V, Debut L, Chaumond J, Wolf T
summary: Distilled BERT during pretraining into a 40% smaller model retaining about 97% of its language-understanding performance.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
authors: Guu K, Lee K, Tung Z, Pasupat P, Chang MW
summary: Pretrained a masked LM jointly with a learned neural retriever over Wikipedia, improving open-domain QA with interpretable knowledge access.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Karpukhin V, Oğuz B, Min S, Lewis P, Wu L, Edunov S, et al.
summary: Dual-encoder BERT retriever trained with in-batch negatives that outperformed BM25 for open-domain QA.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Lewis P, Perez E, Piktus A, Petroni F, Karpukhin V, Goyal N, et al.
summary: RAG: combined a DPR retriever with a BART generator end to end, grounding generation in retrieved documents; the basis of retrieval-augmented LLM systems.

title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
authors: Su J, Lu Y, Pan S, Murtadha A, Wen B, Liu Y
summary: Rotary position embedding (RoPE) encodes relative position by rotating queries and keys, now standard in most LLMs and the basis of context extension.

title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
authors: Borgeaud S, Mensch A, Hoffmann J, Cai T, Rutherford E, Millican K, et al.
summary: RETRO: chunked cross-attention to a 2-trillion-token retrieval database let a 7.5B model match far larger LMs.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
authors: Hu EJ, Shen Y, Wallis P, Allen-Zhu Z, Li Y, Wang S, et al.
summary: Freezes pretrained weights and trains low-rank update matrices, cutting fine-tuning memory and storage by orders of magnitude; the dominant PEFT method.

title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
authors: Frantar E, Ashkboos S, Hoefler T, Alistarh D
summary: One-shot second-order weight quantization to 3-4 bits for GPT-scale models, enabling LLM inference on single GPUs.

title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
authors: Leviathan Y, Kalman M, Matias Y
summary: A small draft model proposes tokens that the large model verifies in parallel, giving 2-3x speedups with identical output distribution.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
authors: Dettmers T, Pagnoni A, Holtzman A, Zettlemoyer L
summary: Backpropagates through a 4-bit NormalFloat quantized model into LoRA adapters, enabling 65B fine-tuning on a single 48GB GPU.

title: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking Multimodal Understanding across Millions of Tokens of Context
authors: Gemini Team, Google
summary: MoE multimodal model with near-perfect recall over contexts of up to 10M tokens across text, audio and video.

title: Gemini 2.5: Pushing the Frontier with Advanced Reasoning, Multimodality, Long Context, and Next Generation Agentic Capabilities
authors: Comanici G, et al.
summary: Thinking-enabled Gemini models combining million-token context, native multimodality and agentic capabilities.

title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation
authors: Li J, Li D, Xiong C, Hoi S
summary: Unified vision-language encoder-decoder pretraining with caption bootstrapping to clean noisy web image-text data.

title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
authors: Alayrac JB, Donahue J, Luc P, Miech A, Barr I, Hasson Y, et al.
summary: Bridged frozen vision encoders and LLMs with gated cross-attention and a perceiver resampler, enabling few-shot multimodal in-context learning on interleaved image-text.

title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
authors: Li J, Li D, Savarese S, Hoi S
summary: A lightweight Querying Transformer connects frozen image encoders to frozen LLMs, giving strong VLMs at low training cost.

title: Visual Instruction Tuning
authors: Liu H, Li C, Wu Q, Lee YJ
summary: LLaVA: connected CLIP to an LLM with a projection and tuned on GPT-4-generated visual instruction data, a simple recipe behind open multimodal assistants.

title: GPT-4V(ision) System Card
authors: OpenAI
summary: Deployment of GPT-4 with image input, bringing general visual understanding to a widely used assistant.

title: Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models
authors: Gemini Team, Google
summary: Natively multimodal models trained jointly on text, images, audio and video, reporting the first human-expert-level MMLU score.

title: Hello GPT-4o
authors: OpenAI
summary: End-to-end omni model processing text, audio and vision in one network, enabling real-time spoken conversation.
